newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt detains 40 Moslem Brotherhood members.
newsitem.headline: Egypt detains 40 Moslem Brotherhood members.

text.p: Egyptian police on Thursday detained 40 members of the outlawed and influential Moslem Brotherhood organisation on charges of plotting ways to spread their ideology, sources at the prosecutor's office said.

They said the men -- doctors, lawyers and college students -- were picked up at the Cairo suburb of Helwan and the nearby town of Tibeen. Six students were released temporarily to sit for their college exams, the sources said.

The prosecution is interrogating the group members who are charged with using the headquarters of the opposition Labour party in Helwan and Tibeen to "plot and plan ways to penetrate labour and student unions to spread their ideology".
Police also seized leaflets spelling out the group's goals, the sources added.
The Moslem Brotherhood is Egypt's oldest fundamentalist Islamist group.
The group is seeking to transform the country into a strict Islamic state by political means and has been keen to distance itself from the Moslem militant group fighting to overthrow the govrnment.

The organisation was tolerated in the past but Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has in recent years equated them to the Moslem militants trying to oust his rule since 1992. Almost 1,000 people have been killed in the political violence.
Egypt has jailed several prominent members of the Brotherhood, rounding up several before parliamentary elections in November 1995.
